answer: Proposed archive gate: each ID stores a distinct ID-encoded 1 GB replica of onyx, velvet and yarrow scans. Validators check replication proofs and random timed retrievals; failure revokes listing. Replication soundness and deadlines excluding regeneration are essential; fast re-encoding can defeat enforcement. Ten concurrent IDs need 10 GB despite shared disks or parallel audits; no replica backs two IDs. Capacity-time is the recurring burden; disks are reusable capital; no stake. Spare capacity makes IDs cheap. This meters storage, not owners.
